title: Activity, Task, Package, and Window Manager Boundaries

scout.purpose: Understand activity, task, package, and window manager boundaries as a causal Android engineering system rather than a vocabulary item.
scout.realWorldUse: Expert Android diagnosis requires tracing responsibility through processes, framework services, threads, queues, graphics buffers, and system composition.
scout.outcome: You can explain, inspect, test, and safely apply activity, task, package, and window manager boundaries.

blocks.text: ActivityManager coordinates process importance and many component or service operations. ActivityTaskManager owns activities, tasks, stacks or display-area organization, launch policy, and task transitions. PackageManager owns installed package metadata, components, permissions, signatures, and intent resolution. WindowManager owns window tokens, focus, input relationships, layout, transitions, z-order, and display policy. These responsibilities collaborate through internal interfaces; no single manager owns the entire path from launcher intent to pixels.

blocks.text: An intent first requires package and component resolution under visibility, exported, permission, user, and policy constraints. Task policy then determines reuse, creation, launch mode, display, and transition. Process state may require ActivityManager and Zygote work. The application later requests a window associated with an authorised activity token; WindowManager validates and positions it and coordinates surfaces. Confusing a task with a process or a window with an activity leads to wrong back-stack, lifecycle, and rendering explanations.

blocks.code: adb shell dumpsys package dev.droidquest; adb shell dumpsys activity activities; adb shell dumpsys activity processes; adb shell dumpsys window windows
blocks.caption: A focused inspection or implementation fragment; interpret it within its process, thread, lifecycle, security, and version context.

blocks.text: Use dumpsys package, activity activities, activity processes, window windows, and Perfetto or Winscope to inspect a controlled launch. Correlate tokens, component names, task IDs, PIDs, windows, and surfaces but expect internal output to vary by Android release. Build a responsibility sequence rather than memorising classes. When diagnosing, ask which service owns the disputed fact, which identity and token authorise it, and which asynchronous callback communicates the next state.

Platform internals are a causal map for diagnosis, not an invitation to depend on hidden APIs. Trace ownership across process, thread, Binder, token, queue, buffer, and display boundaries; distinguish public contracts from release-specific implementation. Use AOSP source matching the device branch, Perfetto, dumpsys, logcat, bug reports, and controlled experiments as complementary evidence. Record Android build, device, configuration, process state, workload, and timestamps. Test death, cancellation, reentrancy, backpressure, configuration, multi-window, and resource pressure. When a private class or trace label changes, the explanation should still stand at the responsibility level. Production apps use supported APIs, while platform changes require compatibility tests, security policy, boot and performance evidence, and safe rollback.

blocks.title: Common systems trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Equating an activity task with a Linux process fails because tasks can outlive processes and one process can host components participating in different task states.

trap_check.mistake: Equating an activity task with a Linux process fails because tasks can outlive processes and one process can host components participating in different task states.
trap_check.why: It collapses distinct ownership or timing boundaries and can produce a confident but incorrect diagnosis.
trap_check.fix: Trace the complete causal path with matching source and runtime evidence before changing the system.

trap_check.mistake: Depending on a hidden API, internal class name, trace label, or one device observation as a stable application contract.
trap_check.why: Platform implementation and vendor behavior can change while public compatibility guarantees remain different.
trap_check.fix: Use internals for explanation and diagnosis, but implement app behavior through supported APIs and test across versions.

challenge_intro.task: Trace a deep-link launch and map resolution, task choice, process need, activity scheduling, window token, focus, surface, and first-frame evidence to service owners.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The result includes a correct causal model, reproducible evidence, adverse-path testing, compatibility boundaries, and an owned regression or recovery plan.

recall.prompt: Which service boundary owns installed component and signature metadata?
recall.answer: PackageManager; task, process, and window services consume that information for their own responsibilities.

recall.prompt: What must be recorded with systems evidence?
recall.answer: The Android and app build, device, configuration, starting state, workload, process or thread context, and exact capture method.

recall.prompt: How should application code use platform-internals knowledge?
recall.answer: Use it to diagnose and reason about public behavior, not to depend on hidden implementation APIs or names.
